notes: Functional, using an optional interface lookup under the series lock with variadic hooks and good tests. It does not address the exemplar-lock vs stripe-lock ordering, and it includes unrelated go.mod/go.sum changes plus a go.work deletion.

It works and passes, but it queries exemplar storage lazily under stripe/series locks without addressing lock order against ChunkSnapshot. It also uses variadic-parameter hacks and carries unrelated go.mod/go.sum/go.work changes.

Clean design: a lock-free precomputed retention set and a gcWithRetain wrapper that keeps gc's signature, with very thorough tests. It is marred by unrelated go.mod/go.sum edits and the deletion of go.work.

This is a clean deadlock-safe design: it precomputes protected label sets, wraps gc as gcWithRetain, and releases chunks with correct metrics. Its tests are very thorough, but the patch includes unrelated go.mod/go.sum edits and deletes go.work.

The retention logic looks reasonable, but it adds a method to the public ExemplarStorage interface and changes the stripeSeries.gc/gcSeries signatures, which breaks compilation against the hidden tests. It also checks the exemplar storage under stripe and series locks (lock-order risk) and adds unrequested walExpiries changes.

It adds an interface method and does a lazy lookup under locks without lock-order mitigation. It also adds unneeded WAL-expiry side effects inside the keep predicate and h.gc, and the gc signature change fails the hidden tests.

Works, using a per-series exemplar-storage lookup under the series lock and rewriting ChunkSnapshot to avoid lock inversion. That rewrite copies all exemplars at shutdown and is broader than needed, as is the general truncateChunksBefore appender change and the variadic hooks.

The lazy per-series storage lookup is made safe by restructuring ChunkSnapshot to collect exemplars before series lookup. It also changes the general behaviour of truncateChunksBefore and relies on variadic hacks, but the tests cover all paths plus zero/negative cutoffs.
Iterates every stored exemplar on each GC and changes the gc/gcSeries signatures (breaking the hidden tests). It also bumps go.mod/go.sum and deletes go.work, which are unrelated changes.

Collecting exemplar-protected label sets up front is deadlock-safe, but changing the gc and gcSeries signatures causes the hidden test failures. It also ships unrelated go.mod/go.sum bumps and deletes go.work.

Precomputes a set of label hashes before locking, which is sensible, but it adds a method to the public ExemplarStorage interface and changes the stripeSeries.gc signature, so the hidden tests fail to compile.

Snapshotting exemplar label hashes up front is a reasonable, deadlock-safe design that is conservative on collisions. It extends the exported ExemplarStorage interface, recomputes hashes instead of reusing the hash parameter, and the required gc signature change breaks the hidden tests.

The logic is careful, including adding chunkSnapshotMtx around truncateOOO. However, it changes the public ExemplarStorage interface and the stripeSeries.gc signature, causing compile failures with the hidden tests.
It extends the exported ExemplarStorage interface and adds a lazy per-series lookup under locks, patching truncateOOO with chunkSnapshotMtx. The required gc signature change breaks the hidden tests.

Closely mirrors the reference: per-series max exemplar time plus a has-exemplar flag, set on commit, WAL replay and snapshot load; a keep hook on stripeSeries; chunks, appender and mmap-ready count released correctly. It marks at commit rather than at append, leaving a tiny race window, and the tests are excellent.

It uses a memSeries hasExemplar/maxExemplarTime approach that matches the reference, updated on commit, replay and snapshot, and hooks in through a keepIfEmpty field so internal signatures stay unchanged. Tests broadly cover all requirements, though it does not protect exemplars before commit.

Snapshots the exemplar-bearing label sets before taking locks, which avoids lock inversion and handles hash collisions. It relies on a type assertion to the circular exemplar storage and a variadic-param hack, and its tests skip AppenderV2, the memory snapshot and the second restart.

It builds a hash-keyed set of exemplar series before taking locks, with full label comparison on collisions, and releases chunks correctly. The variadic parameter is hacky, and the tests skip snapshot, AppenderV2 and second-restart coverage.

Per-series exemplar tracking close to the reference, using a state flag bit and set on commit, replay and snapshot, with correct chunk release. Its new test is inserted between an existing test's doc comment and that test, a comment on chunk IDs is inaccurate, and marking happens at commit time.

It mirrors the reference by tracking the exemplar max timestamp via a state flag, updating it at commit, replay and snapshot, keeping series in gc and releasing chunks in gcSeries. The new head test was inserted so that it steals the existing test's doc comment.

The per-series flag approach is sound, but it changes the stripeSeries.gc/gcSeries signatures (breaking the hidden tests) and never clears series.app on the ordinary gc path, so the removed chunk stays referenced in memory.

The design is close to the reference: it tracks the max exemplar timestamp on memSeries and updates it at commit, WAL replay and snapshot load. However, it changes the required signature of stripeSeries.gc, which breaks the hidden tests, and the gc path never clears the stale appender.
